tool.name: @BINARY@
tool.description: compute pairwise correlations between multiple Hi-C contact matrices
tool.command:
@multiple_input_matrices@ @BINARY@
--matrices $matrices --labels $mlabels
#if $method_cond.method and $method_cond.method is not None: --method $method_cond.method #end if #if $method_cond.method == 'scc': --sccSmoothWindow $method_cond.sccSmoothWindow --sccMaxDistance $method_cond.sccMaxDistance $method_cond.sccDownsample #else if $method_cond.method == 'genomedisco': --genomediscoTmin $method_cond.genomediscoTmin --genomediscoTmax $method_cond.genomediscoTmax $method_cond.genomediscoNoSubsample #else if $method_cond.method == 'hicspector': --hicspectorNumEvec $method_cond.hicspectorNumEvec --hicspectorIprCut $method_cond.hicspectorIprCut #else if $method_cond.method == 'quasar': --quasarWidth $method_cond.quasarWidth #else if $method_cond.method == 'ent3c': --ent3cSubmatrixSize $method_cond.ent3cSubmatrixSize --ent3cChromosomeSplit $method_cond.ent3cChromosomeSplit --ent3cWindowShift $method_cond.ent3cWindowShift --ent3cMaxWindows $method_cond.ent3cMaxWindows --threads \${GALAXY_SLOTS:-4} #end if $log1p #if str($zMin) != '': --zMin $zMin #end if #if str($zMax) != '': --zMax $zMax #end if $plotNumbers
@USE_RANGE@
#if $chromosomes: --chromosomes #echo "' '".join([ "'%s'" % $chrom.chromosome for $chrom in $chromosomes ])# #end if
#if $colormap: --colorMap $colormap #end if
--outFileNameHeatmap heatmap.png --outFileNameScatter scatter.png
## scc/genomedisco/hicspector/quasar/ent3c have no per-bin vectors to ## scatter-plot (hicCorrelate.cpp: "outFileNameScatter is still ## required but left untouched"), so the file is never written ## by the tool for those methods; make sure the declared output ## dataset still exists. && touch -a scatter.png

param.label: Smoothing window half-size
param.help: Half-size of the 2D mean filter used to smooth the matrices before computing SCC (hicrep's --h). 0 disables smoothing. hicrep's own guidance: roughly 200000 / bin size, e.g. 20 at 10kb, 10 at 25kb, 5 at 40kb bins.

param.label: Maximum distance from the diagonal (bp)
param.help: Only consider contacts at most this many bp from the diagonal (hicrep's --dBPMax). -1 uses the whole chromosome. The original HiCRep paper used 5000000 for the human genome.

param.label: Downsample instead of normalize
param.help: Downsample the matrix with more contacts to the other's total instead of normalizing each by its own total (hicrep's --bDownSample).

param.label: Minimum random-walk step
param.help: GenomeDISCO's --tmin: the first random-walk step whose score counts toward the reported value.

param.label: Maximum random-walk step
param.help: GenomeDISCO's --tmax: the last random-walk step. GenomeDISCO's own recommended standard configuration uses tmin = tmax = 3.

param.label: Do not downsample to the lower-depth matrix
param.help: GenomeDISCO's recommended standard configuration downsamples the higher-depth matrix to the lower-depth one's total contacts before normalizing. Check this to normalize by each matrix's own total instead.

param.label: Number of Laplacian eigenpairs to compare
param.help: HiC-Spector's own num_evec: how many of the normalized Laplacian's smallest eigenpairs to compare.

param.label: Inverse-participation-ratio cutoff
param.help: HiC-Spector's own ipr_cut: an eigenvector is only compared if its inverse participation ratio (a delocalization measure) exceeds this.

param.label: Half-window size (bins)
param.help: hifive's own hardcoded width: how many bins on each side a bin's background-corrected contact profile covers, and the largest genomic distance (in bins) two positions can be compared at.

param.label: Submatrix size (bins)
param.help: ENT3C's SUB_M_SIZE_FIX: the dimension of the submatrices along the diagonal. 0 derives it from the chromosome split.

param.label: Chromosome split
param.help: ENT3C's CHRSPLIT: the submatrix size is the number of non-empty bins of a chromosome divided by this value, rounded. 7 is the default of the ENT3C publication.

param.label: Window shift (bins)
param.help: ENT3C's phi: the shift between consecutive submatrices. It is raised until there are at most the maximum number of submatrices.

param.label: Maximum number of submatrices per chromosome
param.help: ENT3C's PHI_MAX: the largest number of values of the entropy signal of a chromosome. 0 sets no limit.

param.label: Use the log1p of the matrix values
param.help: If set, then the log1p of the matrix values is used. This parameter has no effect for Spearman correlations but changes the output of Pearson correlation and, for the scatter plot, if set, the visualization of the values is easier. Ignored for scc/genomedisco/hicspector/quasar/ent3c.

param.label: Minimum value of the heatmap colour scale
Maximum value of the heatmap colour scale
Print the correlation values on the heatmap

repeat.name: chromosomes
repeat.title: List of chromosomes to be included in the correlation

tool.help:
Matrix correlation ==================
**hicCorrelate** is a dedicated Quality Control tool that allows the correlation of multiple Hi-C matrices at once with either a heatmap or scatterplots output.
Computes pairwise correlations between Hi-C matrices data. The correlation is computed taking the values from each pair of matrices and discarding values that are zero in both matrices. Parameters that strongly affect correlations are bin size of the Hi-C matrices (can be changed using ``hicMergeMatrixBins``) and the considered range. The smaller the bin size of the matrices, the finer the differences you score. The *Range* parameter should be selected at a meaningful genomic scale according to, for example, the mean size of the TADs in the organism you work with or to specific ranges found using ``hicPlotDistVsCounts``.
_________________
Usage -----
It is recommended to use this tool on corrected matrices (``hicCorrectMatrix``) at restriction enzyme resolution (unmerged bins).
In addition to Pearson and Spearman, five reproducibility measures are available: **SCC** (HiCRep's stratum-adjusted correlation coefficient), **GenomeDISCO**, **HiC-Spector**, **QuASAR-Rep** and **ENT3C** (an entropy-based similarity). Each uses the same clustering and heatmap as Pearson and Spearman and reports the mean of its score over the chromosomes. They only accept cool/mcool input, ignore *Use the log1p of the matrix values* and *Range restriction*, and produce no scatter plot; the scatter plot output is still produced, but empty.
ENT3C removes the bins that are empty in any of the given matrices before comparing them, so the score of a pair can change with the other matrices given.
_________________
Output ------
**hicCorrelate** outputs correlation plots of multiple Hi-C matrices.
Below, you can find a correlation example of uncorrected Hi-C matrices obtained from *Drosophila melanogaster* embryos, either wild-type or having one gene knocked-down by RNAi.
Heatmap _______
.. image:: $PATH_TO_IMAGES/hicCorrelate_Dmel_heatmap.png :width: 45%
This example is showing a heatmap that was calculated using the Pearson correlation of corrected Hi-C matrices with a bin size of 6000 bp at a range of 5000 to 200000. The dendrogram indicates which samples are most similar to each other. You can see that the wild-type samples are seperated from the knock-down samples. In that case, Spearman correlation gives very similar results (not shown).
Scatterplot ___________
.. image:: $PATH_TO_IMAGES/hicCorrelate_Dmel_scatterplot.png :width: 45%
Additionally, pairwise scatterplots comparing interactions between each sample can be plotted.
_________________
For more information about HiCExplorer please consider our documentation on readthedocs.io_.
.. _readthedocs.io: http://hicexplorer.readthedocs.io/en/latest/index.html .. _Colormap: https://matplotlib.org/examples/color/colormaps_reference.html
